technique.name: Raycasting
technique.description: A ray projected from the user intersects a target for fast distal selection.
technique.best: Fast selection of visible distant targets.
technique.limits: Small and occluded targets can be difficult; precision decreases with distance.
technique.how: Point a virtual ray at an object and confirm with a button, pinch, or dwell.
technique.citation: Mine, M. (1995). Virtual environment interaction techniques. UNC Chapel Hill CS Dept, 2.

technique.name: Virtual Hand
technique.description: A direct 3D selection technique where the user controls a virtual hand to touch, grab, and manipulate nearby objects in the virtual environment.
technique.best: Natural selection and manipulation of nearby objects, especially when the interaction benefits from proprioception and direct hand-object contact.
technique.limits: Less suitable for distant targets because the user must reach toward the object or rely on an extended mapping. It can also cause fatigue during repeated or long interactions.
technique.how: Move the tracked hand or controller so that the virtual hand overlaps with the target object, then confirm the selection by grabbing, pressing a button, or performing a pinch gesture.
technique.citation: Mine, M. R., Brooks Jr, F. P., & Sequin, C. H. (1997, August). Moving objects in space: exploiting proprioception in virtual-environment interaction. In Proceedings of the 24th annual conference on Computer graphics and interactive techniques (pp. 19-26).

technique.name: Cone Casting
technique.description: A cone-shaped volume expands the effective acquisition area for remote targets.
technique.best: Distant targets when exact ray alignment is demanding.
technique.limits: May create ambiguity when several candidates fall inside the cone.
technique.how: Aim a cone at a region; resolve the chosen object by proximity or ranking.

technique.name: Bubble Cursor
technique.description: An adaptive cursor expands until it encloses the nearest available target.
technique.best: Dense scenes with many small selectable objects.
technique.limits: Can feel unpredictable when target positions change quickly.
technique.how: Move the cursor near a target; the selection region adapts to isolate it.

technique.name: Gaze + Pinch
technique.description: Gaze identifies an intended object and a pinch confirms the action.
technique.best: Hands-busy contexts and lightweight XR input.
technique.limits: May suffer from Midas-touch effects without deliberate confirmation.
technique.how: Look at a candidate target, then pinch to select it.
technique.citation: Pfeuffer, K., Mayer, B., Mardanbegi, D., & Gellersen, H. (2017, October). Gaze+ pinch interaction in virtual reality. In Proceedings of the 5th symposium on spatial user interaction (pp. 99-108).

technique.name: VoiceRay
technique.description: Ray-based selection enhanced with ordinal voice commands to resolve ambiguity.
technique.best: Dense and clustered distant objects where raycasting is ambiguous.
technique.limits: Speech latency and social or contextual appropriateness can matter.
technique.how: Aim at a cluster, then say an ordinal command such as “third”.
technique.citation: Turkmen, R., Rasoulifar, Z., & Batmaz, A. U. (2026, April). VoiceRay: 3D Object Selection Technique for Occluded and Dense Environments in Virtual Reality. In Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (pp. 1-19).

technique.name: Aperture Selection
technique.description: Targets are acquired through a controllable aperture that balances precision and speed.
technique.best: Precise selection of small or distant objects.
technique.limits: Requires learning and can add extra adjustment steps.
technique.how: Adjust an aperture around the intended target, then confirm.

technique.name: Volumetric Hand Cursor
technique.description: A 3D cursor volume attached to the hand enables direct spatial selection.
technique.limits: Arm fatigue and occlusion can increase in long sessions.
technique.how: Move a hand-aligned cursor volume to intersect a target, then pinch.

technique.name: Gaze + Voice
technique.description: Gaze narrows the candidate set while voice specifies the final intended item.
technique.best: Highly ambiguous scenes, especially when targets overlap.
technique.limits: Depends on reliable speech recognition and concise labels.
technique.how: Look toward the target group and speak a target name or ordinal.
